title: The Hidden Castle
text: “Nano, it’s surprising that there’s a gimmick like this.”
“The activation method being ‘the heroes turn into pioneer creatures and give each other shoulder rides in front of the island’s monument’ is a joke that’s gone too far.”
“Yeah. Motoyasu was being extremely troublesome about it.”
What’s that supposed to mean? I did it in earnest, I say. Watching Father climb up onto my shoulders gave me a strange, thrilling sense of transgression, indeed.

“Ahaha… well, considering that Rafuemon and the others staying silent seems to mean we’re supposed to finish this island’s events without interfering… maybe this island’s energy or something gets put to good use somewhere, leading to advances in science and technology?”
“Um…”
The one called Rafuemon fell silent, looking troubled, as if unable to answer.
“Sounds like that’s close to correct. Setting Rafuemon-san aside, it’s quite likely this event is a necessary element for Rafumi-san and Filoko-san to be created.”
“Should we cancel here and go home…”
Ren muttered, turning his face toward the main island of Cal Mira.
“Do you intend to live your whole life as a pioneer creature? Honestly… making us walk through such a pointless process, I say.”
“This event doesn’t happen in the very first world Motoyasu-kun and Gaelion-chan know about, right? Which means our loop’s future might end up looking quite different.”

“Nano, that possibility can’t be denied. To begin with, in the loop where Gaelion and the Shield Hero fell mutually in love, the Bow Hero dies, so things related to descendants should be significantly different too, nano.”
Guh… I recalled Father’s face from that loop. Ah… Father. Please forgive me for failing to understand your forward-thinking wisdom back then, I say.

“In the loop where Gaelion-san defeated Motoyasu-san… forgive me for saying so, but it seems like it’d end up a world where demi-humans and beastmen dominate, right? Or rather, monsters having the advantage, I suppose? Gaelion-san is self-proclaimed Demon Lord, after all.”

“Even Gaelion herself can’t fully grasp it now, nano, but Gaelion fully intended to govern properly until death, nano. Considering that, the possibility can’t be ruled out that, starting from Gaelion’s descendants, it became a world favorable to monsters, nano.”
Guh… are you telling me that world fell into Rival’s hands because it defeated me in that loop, Father!? That’s a dark future, I say!
“Don’t tell me Filolial-sama went extinct entirely in that loop! Rival!”
I pointed my spear at Rival, and Rival let out a sigh.
“Don’t underestimate Gaelion, nano. Destroying the Filolials would make Gaelion no better than Takt, nano. As Demon Lord, Gaelion generously tolerates the Filolials’ existence, nano.”
“So as fellow monsters, you view them equally, huh. Even though you’re archenemies.”
“Honestly speaking, dragons don’t actually hate Filolials, nano. It’s just that the other side comes at us hostile, so we rival back, nano.”
Rival was showing such composure! Filolial-sama will never lose, I say, absolutely!
“No telling how different the futures across the different loops might be, but I suppose we just have to keep going…”
“Wonder which world ends up with the best future. Not that it’s something to compare, but maybe thinking that way, it’s best we just keep doing what we can.”
As we talked, a building that looked like a temple came into view.
“Motoyasu-san. It’s not there. Apparently our destination is the castle over here.”
“Oh? Was that so? Is there a castle around, I wonder?”
“Seems there’s a buried castle hidden away somewhere… ah, there it is.”

Deeper into the island, a castle like the one on the main island stood towering, glowing crackling red. It was protected by something resembling a barrier crackling with sparks, and it seemed we could enter through the central gate.
“You’d think something like that underwater would be spotted instantly.”
“Given that no one found it, I suppose that means it really was hidden.”
Talking amongst ourselves, we approached the gate and tried to open it, but it was shut fast. It was a gate with a conspicuous large emblem and a crystal set into it.
“Can’t get in?”

As Father tilted his head, light shot out from our weapons, crossing with the light of the crystal, and there came the click of a lock. As if to double-check, we placed our hands on the gate again, and this time it opened easily.
“Hero authentication, multiple times over.”
“Right. And apparently there’s a way back to normal somewhere inside this castle… would be nice if we found it right away, but…”

Once inside the castle, we couldn’t find anything that looked like what we needed, but we emerged into an elaborately decorated hall. As expected, there were four emblems and… a door leading to the next room, with a large crystal embedded above it. In the center, hanging from a stone tablet, was something resembling the departure lantern we’d seen in the previous dungeon. The four emblems each represented sword, spear, bow, and shield, and scattered among them were icons modeled after the Seven Star Weapons as well. Around the shield emblem were decorations of a hammer and claws. And connected to each emblem were four round circles.
“Would be nice if this tablet had the way back to normal written on it…”
We turned our eyes to the stone tablet where the lantern hung. Then, letters rose up glowing from the tablet.

『Owners of the Sacred Weapons and Vassal Weapons, well done for making your way to this castle upon Cal Mira Island, the land of training, pen. This is a place of further training, a place to store power for the time to come, a place where various weapons and arms sleep, pen. To awaken the memories of your weapons, you must overcome trials of illusions of various monsters, pen.』

Along with this preamble came the rules of this building, it seemed. Apparently it was divided into zones, and once you passed through a zone, any monsters you’d defeated would revive so you could fight them again. Also, only one person could enter this labyrinth at a time, but by using the lantern, you could communicate with whoever was standing in the circle here and instantly swap places with them. What’s more, there seemed to be a separate Level system within the dungeon. Our existing Levels wouldn’t carry over inside the dungeon, apparently… how troublesome, I say.
“Ahh… so this time it’s basically a one-person-at-a-time challenge, but with a party-swap system allowed. Feels like I’ve seen this gimmick somewhere before.”
“How far are you going to run with the meta jokes!”
“Nano, can Gaelion and the others participate in this too?”
“Looks like you’d have to be a pioneer creature to manage it… going by the text on the tablet.”
“That’s troubling, nano.”
“So Yuki and the others are on standby duty again?”
“This time it seems we’ll be able to watch how you’re all doing.”
“Yuki-chan! We can chat while you’re on standby, I say!”
“Motoyasu-sama, we’ll be cheering you on!”
This time it seemed to be the kind of dungeon we could settle in and tackle properly, which was reassuring, I say.
“Lots of new discoveries, kyu…”
Riska was carefully checking over the surrounding mechanisms.
“I’ll help too. Should I report to Mother right away? But Mother is also a Vassal Weapon hero — what if the moment she sets foot on the island, she turns into a pioneer creature too?”
“Even Melty-chan is saying things that aren’t funny at all.”
“Looking at the emblems and decorations here, it’s entirely plausible.”
The idea that being a hero might grant qualification for this was rather frightening, I say.
“It’d be nice if Rishia-san could tinker around and hack the system somehow, but either way, it seems like all we need is one representative to go, so we have no choice but to proceed.”
With that, Itsuki stepped onto the circle marked with the bow. At once, the circle glowed softly, and the emblem lit up.
“Nano, it’s nice just to see something with a different flavor from last time. Gaelion will investigate the flow of mana and the Dragon Vein while at it, nano.”
“Everyone on the technical team, I’m counting on you. Now then, Naofumi-san, everyone, please take your positions properly.”
“Another unknown event, but I suppose we’ve no choice but to proceed.”

With a sigh, Ren stepped onto the circle connected to the sword emblem. Father and I followed suit and stepped on as well, and once the lights aligned… there came a click, and the door opened. At the same time, the lock on the lantern came undone, allowing it to be taken.
“So, who’s going first, I wonder?”
“I’ll go, I say!”
Itsuki and Ren both turned to look at me, furrowing their brows, but then nodded with a sigh.
